title: Lodging Tax Advisory Committee Grant Program Guidelines (2026 Update, 2027 cycle)
why: Splits funding into four categories with stated targets and past award ranges (Cultural Enrichment near $5,000, Large Event/Festival needing 2,500+ attendance and capped at two repeat awards unless attendance grows 20%). Lists scoring priorities such as off-peak timing, areas outside downtown and 50+ mile visitors, so applicants know what wins.

title: 2027 Lodging Tax Grant Guidelines
why: Sets a 25% minimum match, reimbursement-only payment and a three-consecutive-year funding limit that pushes events toward self-sufficiency. Requires a year-end table of predicted vs actual attendance and paid lodging nights with the collection method for each figure.

title: Tourism Grant Application page (cycle due Sept 4, 2026, contracts Jan 2027)
why: Three tiers with clear caps and terms (Visitor-Generating Events up to $100,000 a year on a two-year contract, Destination Experience up to $35,000, Small Grant up to $5,000) and published point weights for each tier. Links a Hotel Collaboration Form and requires pre and post marketing meetings with the DMO.

title: Lodging Tax (Hotel-Motel Tax) topic page
why: Plain summary of RCW 67.28 eligible uses, LTAC membership rules, the 45-day review requirement and JLARC reporting, plus a list of sample codes, RFPs and recipient contracts from Washington cities. A good first read for staff setting up or auditing a program.

title: FY 2025-26 Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT) Grant Application Manual
why: One manual holds eligibility, caps (capital grants up to $20,000 and 50% of cost), a 25-point rubric per grant type with a stated passing band of 18.75, and the completion report forms. The event rubric scores grant cost per attendee in dollar bands (under $10 earns full points).

title: 2026 Visitor Experience Grant Guidelines
why: Lodging-tax-funded capital and visitor experience grants of $25,000 to $50,000 from a $200,000 pool, with a clear ineligible list (events, marketing campaigns, salaries) and a three-consecutive-year limit. Unused funds must be returned and future funding depends on completed reporting.

title: 2025-2026 TLT Tourism-Related Facilities Grant Information
why: Applies the ORS 320.300 definition of a tourism-related facility (10+ year useful life) to a $400,000 pool with a $75,000 cap. Publishes five weighted criteria including destination management and return on investment, and requires quarterly progress reports.

title: Destination Events and Programming Grants, 2026-2027 Grant Cycle Guidelines
why: Small-city model that ties the award cap to the calendar: up to $5,000 for October to mid-March events, $3,000 for shoulder dates, and summer weeks excluded. Rolling monthly review, priority for programs likely to fill local hotel rooms, and unused funds can be recalled.

title: Lodging Local Option Tax program page
why: Lists the eight voter-approved purposes an applicant must match, the March 1 to April 30 window and the Local Option Tax Commission review. Links multi-year funding recommendations and a funding-by-recipient history, a transparency practice other resort cities can copy.

title: 2027 LTAC Scoring Matrices
why: Five matrices, one per funding category, each scored 1 to 5 per criterion with a 60% minimum to be considered (for example 42 of 70 for Event Marketing). Each sets a room-night floor, such as 300 peak or 500 total for event marketing, so applicants can self-screen before applying.

title: Scoring Rubric for Lodging Tax Grant Applications (2026 cycle)
why: Publishes point bands for every criterion, including paid lodging nights (1 point under 25, 5 points over 200, plus a bonus for having the DMO verify the estimate) and seasonality (4 points for December to February). Applicants can score themselves line by line.

title: 2027 Lodging Tax Funding Scoring Rubric
why: 160-point rubric where two criteria are scored automatically from the application (frequency and location) and two by evaluators. Tourism promotion gives 50 points only for drawing visitors from 50+ miles and 10 for mostly local crowds.

title: Lodging Tax Advisory Committee Award Criteria (2027 cycle)
why: Each criterion is scored 0 to 4 against written level definitions and multiplied by a weight, with overnight stays and visitor impact at x4 (16 points each of 60). Adds up to 10 bonus points for off-season dates, multi-day programming and outside match.

title: 2026 Hotel/Motel Tax Grant Application Rating Sheet
why: One-page 100-point sheet that gives Hotel Partnerships 15 points and Marketing 15 points, plus a 5-point bonus for September to May projects that generate hotel stays. Simple enough for a small committee to adopt as is.

title: 2026 Tourism and Cultural Investment (TACI) Grant Scoring Guide
why: 100-point guide with guiding questions under each sub-criterion; Impact on Lodging and Tourism carries 30 points, including 10 for lodging utilization and hotel partnerships. Useful for producers writing narrative answers that map to each scored item.

title: Attachment A: Lodging Tax Evaluation Form (2025, for 2026 funds)
why: Uses two yes/no gates (tourism alignment and guideline compliance) before 11 weighted criteria totaling 85 points, with 10 points each for overnight travelers from 50+ miles and the current funding priority. Shows how a county can rotate a priority (here the 2026 FIFA World Cup) into scoring.

title: Bend Cultural Tourism Fund 2026 Marketing Grant Guidelines
why: 100-point rubric with ROI Measurement and Evaluation worth 20 points and a hard 80-point minimum for funding. Excludes July and August activity entirely, a clear way to push grants into the shoulder season.

title: 2027 Lodging Tax Grant Program Master Application
why: One master application plus a sub-application per project keeps data comparable. Requires projected room nights and computes a room-night ROI (room nights x $125 ADR divided by request), and applicants must describe how overnight stays will be generated and tracked.

title: Lodging Tax Grants Application for 2026 Funding: Events and Festivals
why: Asks for total attendees, tourist attendees and estimated commercial room nights with the documentation method, and scores each section (50 points). Includes a Hotel Collaboration Form where the hotel confirms actual room counts within 30 days, and withholds the last 10% until the final report.

title: 2027 Tourism Program Grant Application
why: Requires attendance split into the five state categories plus projected paid lodging nights, the data collection method, its estimated accuracy, and how hotel stays will be verified. Sets a floor that at least 5% of attendance travel 50+ miles and caps the grant at 50% of project cost.

title: 2026 Lodging Tax Grant Funding Request for Proposal
why: Numbered attachment list with page limits, a required Impact on Tourism template, and a budget that must include a plan for a reduced award. Post-event actuals must state how attendance was counted (head count, car count, survey) and accompany the final reimbursement.

title: Application for Fiscal Year 2027 Lodging Tax Grant Funds
why: Explains the split between the 4% general tourism portion and the 3% portion restricted to large convention and attraction facilities, and states existing commitments up front. Applicants must say how a partial award would change the project and later report actuals against their own estimates.

title: Local Option Tax Funding Application FY26
why: Short form for a small resort city that makes applicants pick one of the ten ordinance purposes (Section 3.10.050) and explain the public purpose. Offers upfront allocation or reimbursement, both closed out with a Final Award Report, and requires LOT credit in all advertising.

title: Tourism Grant Hotel/Motel Lodging Tax Report (2026 form)
why: Predicted vs actual for each attendance category and paid lodging nights, with a counting method and explanation required for every line. The form itself defines a lodging night and all five methods (direct count through structured estimate), so recipients do not need a separate guide.

title: 2026-2027-2028 City of SeaTac Lodging Tax Funding Report (after event/program report)
why: Due two weeks after the event with invoices, proof of payment and completion images. Requires predicted and actual paid lodging nights with a method picked from the state list, and states that missing information means no reimbursement and no future applications.

title: Lodging Tax Recipient JLARC Activity Report
why: Small-city version of the state report with projected, actual and methodology columns, and an instruction that projected figures must match the original application. Defines each counting method in plain language on the form.

title: 2025 Poulsbo Tourism Grant Annual Report (online form)
why: Online form that collects the six JLARC fields (predicted, actual, method, explanation) for each funded activity, which lets staff export straight into the state report. A low-effort model for cities without a grants portal.

title: FAQs for Reporting Lodging Tax Expenditures (updated December 2023)
why: Source definitions for the five counting methods used on Washington report forms, and guidance that a good-faith estimate is acceptable when a count is impractical. Advises LTACs to collect the method along with every number.

title: Tourism Grant Program Mid-Term and/or Final Report (fillable)
why: Short Oregon form that compares actual income and expenses to budget, asks for data supporting room nights generated, and requires a check for any unspent grant funds. Shows how a small city closes out a grant on one page.

title: Kittitas County Lodging Tax Advisory Committee By-Laws (May 8, 2024)
why: Bylaws for a consolidated county and city committee: staggered two and three year terms by seat type, majority quorum, a chair who votes only to break ties, and recusal under RCW 42.23 when a proposal would benefit a member. Proposals can go to commissioners with all votes recorded.

title: Federal Way Revised Code Chapter 2.75, Lodging Tax Advisory Committee (amended 2023)
why: Clean code chapter that keeps collector and recipient seats equal, requires conflict disclosure before appointment, has the committee file its bylaws with the clerk, and spells out the 45-day review of tax and use changes.

title: Gig Harbor Municipal Code 2.53.020, LTAC membership (Ord. 1492, 2022)
why: Nine-seat structure with three-year staggered terms (no more than three expiring per year), a three-term limit, holdover until replaced, and annual council review of membership. Useful language for keeping a committee from turning over all at once.

title: Local Option Tax Commission page
why: Defines a resident commission with seats drawn from other city advisory committees, business, a senior representative and at-large residents, and charges it with reviewing all requests and sending an annual budget recommendation to council. A working model for Idaho resort cities without written bylaws.

title: Enrolled House Bill 4148 (2026 Laws, Chapter 121): local transient lodging tax percentages
why: Amends ORS 320.350 so that new or increased local lodging taxes must put at least 50% (down from 70%) into tourism promotion or tourism-related facilities, operative January 1, 2027. Any Oregon city drafting or amending a 70/30 ordinance should start here.

title: Ordinance No. 1477 establishing a Transient Room Tax (Chapter 3.50)
why: Short, clean example of the 70/30 split under ORS 320.350: 70% of net proceeds to tourism promotion or tourism-related facilities and 30% to city services, with a 5% operator collection fee. Note that HB 4148 lets the split move to 50/50 from 2027.

title: Ordinance 2025-03 revising the Union County Transient Tax Ordinance
why: Writes the allocation into code by percentage (27% tourism promotion, 15% events, 10% discretionary grants, named facilities and public safety shares) and creates a seven-member review committee with set seats. The posted copy has blank reading dates, so confirm the adopted version.

title: Ordinance 2025-01 amending Code 34.15(A), clarifying use of TLT revenue
why: Allocates the tax in tranches: the first 5% across seven council categories with no category above 40%, the next 2% entirely to tourism promotion or facilities, and the remaining 3% consistent with ORS 320.350. Shows how a coastal city documents a pre-2003 split.

title: Chelan County Lodging Tax Framework 2026 (adopted Dec 15, 2025)
why: One-page adopted framework that fixes each recipient's percentage share (27% countywide DMO, 20% each to two chambers and the county, 10% to open event and marketing grants). A simple way to make standing allocations public and predictable.

title: Sample ballot: City of Sandpoint tourist lodging tax increase (Nov 8, 2022)
why: Resort city ballot language that states the rate change (7% to 14%), the end date (Dec 31, 2035) and how each half of the revenue will be used, including an estimate for the new half. A plain model for Idaho cities drafting a lodging LOT question.

title: Lodging Tax Fund (LTAC): 2026 Approvals
why: Lists every applicant with requested and approved amounts, grouped by category (tourism promotion, events, capital, admin) with category totals of $3.53M approved. Easy for producers to benchmark typical event awards against requests.

title: Summary of 2026 Lodging Tax Funding Requests and LTAC Funding Recommendations
why: Shows all 20 requests ($1.36M) beside the $450,000 recommended and council-approved on Feb 25, 2026, which makes the level of competition and typical cut visible to applicants.

title: LTAC scoring sheet: recommendations to council for 2026 awards
why: Publishes each reviewer's score, the average, prior-year funding, the request and the consensus amount for every applicant. Rare example of a committee showing how scores turned into dollars.

title: 2026 LTAC Event and Marketing Grants memo to the Board
why: 43 small event and marketing awards from $500 to $20,000 totaling $221,638, listed by applicant and event. Good reference for what a county open-grant pool funds at the small end.

title: Cultural and Tourism Promotion Advisory Board packet, March 12, 2024 (FY2025 recommended awards)
why: Lists every applicant with requested amount, average score and recommendation, and shows which fell below the 18.75 passing score. Also shows how the board fit $851,670 of passing requests into $791,970 available.

title: News release: 2025-26 Tourism Facilities Grant awards (Feb 4, 2026)
why: Names all 12 facility projects with amounts ($453,425 total), from restrooms and trails to a lighthouse lens. Shows how a county DMO reports TLT facilities spending to the public.

title: 2024 Lodging Tax Expenditures briefing report (July 2025)
why: Statewide roll-up of what 194 municipalities reported: $114M awarded, 1,743 activities, 38M paid-lodging attendees and 24M paid lodging nights. Useful baseline for a city comparing its own results and reporting compliance.

title: Lodging Tax Funding History 2023-2026
why: Four-year table of requests vs funding by organization alongside tax proceeds, program spending and ending fund balance. A compact format for showing council the fund's health before setting the next award level.

title: Travel Salem 2025-26 Second Quarter Report to the City of Salem
why: Contract-required DMO report (City contract Section 1.8) with booked and actual room nights, TOT collections year to date, occupancy and ADR, and website and leverage results against goals. Shows what a city should expect back for its TOT money.

title: FY 2027 Budget Development: Local Option Tax (council memo and slides, Mar 25, 2026)
why: Shows council each LOT-funded agency's amount for FY2024 through the FY2027 starting point, plus air service funding, before budget decisions. A clear multi-year view that Idaho resort cities rarely publish.

title: Visit Sun Valley 2024-2025 Annual Report
why: Publishes revenue by source (including $1.6M from the LOT-funded Air Service Board), expenses by line (advertising $973,068), and seasonal occupancy and visitor center results. A model for the public accounting a LOT-funded DMO should give its funders.

jurisdiction: Kittitas County (consolidated with Ellensburg, Cle Elum, Roslyn)
title: 2027 Lodging Tax Fund RFP and CLTAC Guide
why: Caps returning applicants at the most they actually spent and were reimbursed last cycle, caps ongoing events at 10% of their expense budget, and lets the committee bar anyone who used under 50% of an award from the next cycle (under 75% must explain why). Clear rules that keep awards tied to real performance.

title: Grant Agreement: Lodging Tax (2025 template)
why: Limits reimbursement to the awarded amount and each approved budget line, allows withholding when the final attendance report (with counting method) is missing, and allows termination without notice if funds are misused. Sets firm spend and proof-of-payment deadlines.

title: Clallam County Tourism Enhancement Grant 2025 Program Guidelines
why: Holds back 5% until all reimbursement paperwork is in, sets a 45-day reimbursement window, limits in-area advertising to 25% of the ad budget, and allows full or partial repayment for noncompliance. Caps awards at $7,500 per project and $15,000 per organization.

title: Policy for the Distribution of Transient Lodging Tax Funds for Destination Management
why: Facility grants are paid by reimbursement draw-downs with quarterly reports, and grantees must hold title for ten years or return all or part of the funds. Also sets the nine-member advisory committee's scoring and ranking process.

title: Lodging Tax Request for Reimbursement form
why: Lists exactly what a payment request needs: itemized request, receipts, proof of payment showing the organization's name, ad samples, and the expenditure reporting worksheet before the final payment. Clear instructions reduce rejected claims.

category: Marketing or DMO contract with deliverables
title: Agreement between the City of Portland and Travel Portland (July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2029)
why: Passes the 1% lodging tax and 3% TID to the DMO with fixed deliverables: two-year strategic plan, quarterly and annual reports to council, audited financials, and eight performance objectives including ROI and room nights from diverse group bookings. Sets 25% of film office money aside for events drawing 50+ mile visitors.

category: Marketing or DMO contract with deliverables
title: RFP 2026-019: Kitsap County Designated Marketing Organization
why: Ties DMO funding to a formula (the greater of $500,000 or 50% of available stadium lodging tax funds) and lists sample KPIs such as 3 to 5% visitor growth and $10 return per $1. Requires data export on termination and a sample annual progress report.

category: Marketing or DMO contract with deliverables
title: Visit Bend contract Exhibit A: Scope of Services
why: Lists DMO duties by area (marketing, destination development, grant administration, research), requires visitation reports to the city's advisory board twice a year and an annual business plan to council, and keeps a rainy day fund equal to 5% of the DMO budget.

category: Marketing or DMO contract with deliverables
title: Amendment 4 to Grant Agreement 5012 with Visit Tillamook Coast (term to June 30, 2027)
why: Sets yearly TLT payments in quarterly installments, requires monthly ledgers and an annual report on benchmarks and unspent TLT balance, and focuses the program on October to mid-May. Includes trademark transfer to the county if the agreement ends.

category: Marketing or DMO contract with deliverables
title: RFP: Tourism Promoter/Coordinator (May 2026)
why: Small-city scope that requires monthly traceable-results reports to the LTAC and an annual report comparing estimated and actual overnight stays, 50+ mile trips and out-of-area visitors. A practical template where a city contracts one promoter instead of a full DMO.
